quote: No. I mean, maybe my wife. I'm not I'd have to look at that, but it it the two of us, we live together, still married.
stewart_read: The customer explicitly says he doesn't know if his wife is on the title. The rep accepts 'no problem' and never circles back to confirm before the appointment is booked, leaving a live co-decision-maker's involvement undetermined at close.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could be deliberately deferring the ownership confirmation to the closer's intake rather than re-litigating it — but there is no evidence the rep flagged this for follow-up or told the closer, so this reads as an oversight rather than a deferred strategic move.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to get a definitive answer on title status before booking — 'let's just double check that together real quick' — rather than letting 'I'd have to look at that' pass as resolved.

quote: Mhmm. Yeah. No problem. So, yeah, I can try I can give you some information. I don't know, like, as much as a specialist, of course, just because I'm a scheduler.
stewart_read: Rep proactively self-labels as 'a scheduler' and caveats his own program explanation before delivering it — this is a boundary-setting move, not scope creep, since the immediately following content (credit threshold, savings guarantee, state incentives) tracks the qualifiers.credit_qualifier script almost verbatim.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be read as scope creep since the rep is explaining program mechanics unprompted, but the content matches the schema's own credit_qualifier template closely enough that this is compliant verify content, not premature closer-tier material.
coaching_implication: No correction needed here — the rep's self-caveat ('I don't know as much as a specialist') is a good instinct to reinforce, since it manages expectations without ceding scope.

quote: Yeah. Okay. Alright. Yeah. That's good to know. We can definitely help get that cut down. I know that ComEd is they've been raising their rates quite a bit from what I've heard, so I'm glad you guys are looking into an an alternative.
stewart_read: This is the closest the rep gets to a flip — he references ComEd's rising rates and frames solar as 'an alternative' right after the customer states a $150-$270 monthly range. It's directionally aligned with objection_inversion (aligning against the utility) but stays generic ('they've been raising rates from what I've heard') rather than tying the specific dollar figure back to the customer as personal leverage.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be scored as a full flip since the strategy_recognition principle rewards strategy match over verbatim match — but the line never references the customer's actual $150-$270 number, so it's a partial/soft flip rather than a complete bill-anchor-to-action move.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to make the flip specific: reflect the customer's own number back ('so you're seeing $270 in the summer go straight to ComEd — that's what we're aiming to redirect') rather than a general statement about utility rate increases.

quote: And then, yeah, your home looks pretty good for solar. The roof looks good and everything.
stewart_read: The rep asserts a visual roof assessment ('the roof looks good') before asking any roof detail question, which is an authority claim not grounded in anything stated on the call at that point.
alternative_hypothesis: This could be boilerplate rapport filler intended to sound warm rather than a literal claim of visual inspection, but as phrased it reads as an ungrounded assertion of assessment.
coaching_implication: Flag the habit of asserting roof condition before verifying it — ask the age/condition question first, then react to the answer, rather than pre-validating sight unseen.

quote: Yeah. I'm trying to pull up my calendar, but for some reason, my password isn't working. So, I mean, I I usually know the times that are open. So I'll just probably schedule you
stewart_read: Rep hits a genuine technical failure (calendar login) and handles it with transparency rather than stalling silently or inventing false certainty — he tells the customer what's wrong and proposes a concrete workaround immediately.
coaching_implication: This is a positive example worth reinforcing — transparent admission plus immediate recovery kept the booking moving instead of losing momentum.

quote: Yeah. Yeah. So just wanting to look at the different options and, yeah, what what incentives there are.
stewart_read: Customer discloses a prior Ionic purchase conversation that 'wasn't the right fit' and current interest in comparing lease/PPA options — real competitive intelligence about why a prior deal fell through. The rep never asks what specifically didn't fit about the earlier purchase offer.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may be intentionally not re-litigating a stalled deal to avoid reopening a past objection before the closer — but there's no indication he flagged this detail for the closer either, so the probe is simply skipped rather than deliberately deferred.
coaching_implication: A single follow-up question ('what was it about the purchase option that didn't work for you?') would hand the closer a specific reason to pivot to lease/PPA framing instead of repeating the same pitch that already failed once.
